claim: Dengue is the most common arboviral disease to affect humans globally.
source: Dengue is the most common arboviral disease to affect humans globally.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about dengue's global prevalence.

claim: In 2019, the WHO identified dengue as one of the top 10 threats to global health.
source: In 2019, the World Health Organization (WHO) identified dengue as one of the top 10 threats to global health (World Health Organization, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization, 2019.

claim: Dengue transmission occurs in 129 countries.
source: Transmission occurs in 129 countries, with an estimated 3.9 billion people being at risk (World Health Organization, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization, 2020.

claim: An estimated 3.9 billion people are at risk of dengue.
source: Transmission occurs in 129 countries, with an estimated 3.9 billion people being at risk (World Health Organization, 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization, 2020.

claim: Over the last two decades, the number of reported dengue cases per year has increased more than eight-fold.
source: Over the last two decades, the number of reported cases per year has increased more than eight-fold (World Health Organization, 2020)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to the World Health Organization, 2020.

claim: In 2020 the annual number of dengue virus infections was estimated to be 105 million.
source: in 2020 the annual number of dengue virus (DENV) infections was estimated to be 105 million, with 51 million cases being clinically apparent (Cattarino et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cattarino et al., 2020.

claim: In 2020, 51 million dengue cases were clinically apparent.
source: in 2020 the annual number of dengue virus (DENV) infections was estimated to be 105 million, with 51 million cases being clinically apparent (Cattarino et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cattarino et al., 2020.

claim: With climate change, increased travel and urbanization, the rise in dengue cases is forecasted to continue over the coming decades.
source: With climate change, increased travel and urbanization, this rise is forecasted to continue over the coming decades (Whitehorn and Yacoub, 2019; Yacoub et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Whitehorn and Yacoub, 2019 and Yacoub et al., 2011.

claim: There is no specific treatment for dengue.
source: Despite the large disease burden, there is still no specific treatment for dengue
evidence: This is a statement of established medical knowledge about dengue treatment.

claim: The only licensed dengue vaccine is recommended only in individuals with earlier dengue infection.
source: the only licensed vaccine is recommended only in individuals with earlier dengue infection (Redoni et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Redoni et al., 2020.

claim: Most symptomatic dengue infections are self-limiting.
source: Although most symptomatic dengue infections are self-limiting, a small proportion of patients develop complications
evidence: This is a statement of established clinical knowledge about dengue disease course.

claim: A small proportion of dengue patients develop complications.
source: Although most symptomatic dengue infections are self-limiting, a small proportion of patients develop complications
evidence: This is a statement of established clinical knowledge about dengue disease course.

claim: Most dengue complications manifest at around 4–6 days from symptom onset.
source: a small proportion of patients develop complications, most of which manifest at around 4–6 days from symptom onset.
evidence: This is a statement of established clinical knowledge about the timing of dengue complications.

claim: Utility of the 2009 WHO dengue guidelines at identifying those at risk for complications remains limited.
source: Although the 2009 WHO dengue guidelines set out specific warning signs for use in patient triage, utility of these guidelines at identifying those at risk for complications remains limited (Morra et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Morra et al., 2018.

claim: An excessive immune response acting through inflammatory mediators can lead to bleeding, shock, and organ dysfunction in dengue.
source: It is hypothesized that an excessive immune response acting through inflammatory mediators can lead to the observed manifestations of bleeding, shock, and organ dysfunction.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about dengue pathogenesis based on scientific reasoning.

claim: In secondary dengue infections, adaptive immune activation can result in high circulating levels of plasma cytokines and chemokines.
source: Studies have shown that in secondary infections, adaptive immune activation can result in high circulating levels of plasma cytokines and chemokines (Katzelnick et al., 2017; Midgley et al., 2011; Screaton et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Katzelnick et al., 2017; Midgley et al., 2011; Screaton et al., 2015.

claim: Binding of viral NS1 protein onto endothelial cells can act in concert with vasoactive substances, cytokines, and chemokines to result in endothelial activation and glycocalyx disruption.
source: Binding of viral NS1 protein onto endothelial cells can act in concert with vasoactive substances, cytokines, and chemokines, to result in endothelial activation and glycocalyx disruption, and these processes likely underlie the increased vascular permeability and coagulopathy (McBride and Khanh Lam, 2020; Modhiran et al., 2015; St John et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to McBride and Khanh Lam, 2020; Modhiran et al., 2015; St John et al., 2013.

claim: Endothelial activation and glycocalyx disruption likely underlie the increased vascular permeability and coagulopathy in dengue.
source: Binding of viral NS1 protein onto endothelial cells can act in concert with vasoactive substances, cytokines, and chemokines, to result in endothelial activation and glycocalyx disruption, and these processes likely underlie the increased vascular permeability and coagulopathy (McBride and Khanh Lam, 2020; Modhiran et al., 2015; St John et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to McBride and Khanh Lam, 2020; Modhiran et al., 2015; St John et al., 2013, and involves inference about pathogenic mechanisms.

claim: VCAM-1, SDC-1, and Ang-2 represent endothelial activation and glycocalyx integrity.
source: We included vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), syndecan-1 (SDC-1), and angiopoietin-2 (Ang-2) because they represent endothelial activation and glycocalyx integrity (Han et al., 2019; Mapalagamage et al., 2020; Suwarto et al., 2017; Yacoub et al., 2016a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Han et al., 2019; Mapalagamage et al., 2020; Suwarto et al., 2017; Yacoub et al., 2016a.

claim: IL-8 and IP-10 are associated with dengue disease severity.
source: For markers of immune activation, we measured interleukin-8 (IL-8) and interferon gamma-induced protein-10 (IP-10) as these are associated with disease severity (Oliveira et al., 2017; Pandey et al., 2015; Rathakrishnan et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Oliveira et al., 2017; Pandey et al., 2015; Rathakrishnan et al., 2012.

claim: IL-1RA, sCD163, and sTREM-1 are activation markers of monocytes and macrophages.
source: IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA), soluble cluster of differentiation 163 (sCD163), and soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (sTREM-1) as these are activation markers of monocytes and macrophages, the major targets for dengue replication (Ab-Rahman et al., 2016; John et al., 2015; S S et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Ab-Rahman et al., 2016; John et al., 2015; S S et al., 2017.

claim: Monocytes and macrophages are the major targets for dengue replication.
source: IL-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1RA), soluble cluster of differentiation 163 (sCD163), and soluble triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells-1 (sTREM-1) as these are activation markers of monocytes and macrophages, the major targets for dengue replication (Ab-Rahman et al., 2016; John et al., 2015; S S et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about dengue viral tropism, supported by citations to Ab-Rahman et al., 2016; John et al., 2015; S S et al., 2017.

claim: A total of 281 severe/moderate dengue cases and 556 uncomplicated dengue cases were included in the analysis.
source: In total 281 cases and 556 controls were included in the analysis (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study sample size, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: On days 1–3 from symptom onset, higher levels of any biomarker increased the risk of developing severe/moderate dengue.
source: On days 1–3 from symptom onset, higher levels of any biomarker increased the risk of developing S/MD.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis.

claim: When assessing biomarkers together, SDC-1 and IL-1RA were stable in their association with severe/moderate dengue.
source: When assessing together, SDC-1 and IL-1RA were stable, while IP-10 changed the association from positive to negative; others showed weaker associations.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis comparing single and global models.

claim: When assessing biomarkers together, IP-10 changed the association from positive to negative.
source: When assessing together, SDC-1 and IL-1RA were stable, while IP-10 changed the association from positive to negative; others showed weaker associations.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis comparing single and global models.

claim: The best combination of biomarkers associated with severe/moderate dengue in children comprised IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, ferritin, IP-10, and SDC-1.
source: The best combinations associated with S/MD comprised IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, ferritin, IP-10, and SDC-1 for children
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: The best combination of biomarkers associated with severe/moderate dengue in adults comprised SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, sTREM-1, IL-1RA, IP-10, and sCD163.
source: SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, sTREM-1, IL-1RA, IP-10, and sCD163 for adults.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: The IDAMS study was supported by the EU's Seventh Framework Programme (FP7-281803 IDAMS), the WHO, and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.
source: This study was supported by the EU's Seventh Framework Programme (FP7-281803 IDAMS), the WHO, and the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation.
evidence: This is a direct statement about funding sources.

claim: The IDAMS study enrolled 7428 participants in eight countries across Asia and Latin America.
source: There were 7428 participants in eight countries across Asia and Latin America enrolled in the IDAMS study.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the parent study's enrollment.

claim: Patients were eligible for IDAMS inclusion if they were aged 5 years or older, had fever or history of fever for less than 72 hr, and had symptoms consistent with dengue.
source: Patients were eligible for inclusion if they were aged 5 years or older, had fever or history of fever for less than 72 hr, and had symptoms consistent with dengue, with no features strongly suggestive of another disease.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's inclusion criteria.

claim: Laboratory-confirmed dengue was defined by a positive RT-PCR or a positive NS1 ELISA result.
source: Laboratory-confirmed dengue was defined by a positive reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) or a positive NS1 enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) result.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the diagnostic criteria used in the study.

claim: The majority of the patients were from Vietnam (640 cases, 76%).
source: The majority of the patients were from Vietnam (640 cases, 76%).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study population's geographic distribution.

claim: Median age of the case group was 12 years (1st, 3rd quartiles: 9, 22).
source: Median (1st, 3rd quartiles) age of the case and control groups were 12 (9, 22) and 16 (10, 24) years.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the demographic characteristics of the study population.

claim: Median age of the control group was 16 years (1st, 3rd quartiles: 10, 24).
source: Median (1st, 3rd quartiles) age of the case and control groups were 12 (9, 22) and 16 (10, 24) years.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the demographic characteristics of the study population.

claim: Among the severe/moderate dengue group, 127 cases (45%) were children and 154 cases (55%) were adults.
source: Among the S/MD group, 127 cases (45%) were children and 154 cases (55%) were adults.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the age distribution in the case group.

claim: DENV-1 was the predominant serotype (42%).
source: Serotype distribution was similar between the S/MD and control groups, with DENV-1 predominating (42%), particularly in children (48%).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the serotype distribution in the study population.

claim: There was a higher proportion of secondary infections in the severe/moderate dengue group compared with controls (78% versus 64%).
source: Host immune status however differed: there was a higher proportion of secondary infections in the S/MD group compared with controls (78% versus 64%, respectively) and this was consistent in both children and adults.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the immune status distribution between groups.

claim: Hospitalization was more common in the severe/moderate dengue group (57% versus 31%).
source: As expected, hospitalization was more common in the S/MD group (57% versus 31%) (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about hospitalization rates between groups.

claim: Overall, 38 patients developed severe dengue.
source: Overall, 38 patients developed severe dengue, most were severe plasma leakage (33/38 cases, 87%) and 29/38 (76%) were children.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the number of severe dengue cases.

claim: Most severe dengue cases were severe plasma leakage (33/38 cases, 87%).
source: Overall, 38 patients developed severe dengue, most were severe plasma leakage (33/38 cases, 87%) and 29/38 (76%) were children.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the clinical manifestations of severe dengue.

claim: 76% of severe dengue cases (29/38) were children.
source: Overall, 38 patients developed severe dengue, most were severe plasma leakage (33/38 cases, 87%) and 29/38 (76%) were children.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the age distribution of severe dengue cases.

claim: On average, patients who progressed to severe/moderate dengue had higher levels of the biomarkers in both children and adult patients, both at enrollment and at follow-up.
source: On average, the patients who progressed to S/MD had higher levels of the biomarkers in both children and adult patients, both at enrollment and at follow-up (Figure 2, Appendix 4—table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, shown in Figure 2 and Appendix 4—table 2.

claim: For most individuals, the levels of VCAM-1, IL-8, IP-10, IL-1RA, and CRP decreased between enrollment and follow-up.
source: For most individuals, the levels of five biomarkers (VCAM-1, IL-8, IP-10, IL-1RA, and CRP) decreased between enrollment and follow-up
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, shown in Appendix 4—figure 1.

claim: SDC-1 levels increased slightly between enrollment and follow-up.
source: whereas SDC-1 increased slightly and the other markers showed no clear trends (Appendix 4—figure 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis, shown in Appendix 4—figure 1.

claim: Moderate-to-strong positive correlations were evident for IP-10 and IL-1RA (Spearman's rank correlation coefficient above 0.6).
source: Moderate-to-strong positive correlations were evident for some markers, in particular IP-10 and IL-1RA, and IP-10 and VCAM-1, both with Spearman's rank correlation coefficients above 0.6 (Appendix 4—figure 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's correlation analysis, shown in Appendix 4—figure 2.

claim: Moderate-to-strong positive correlations were evident for IP-10 and VCAM-1 (Spearman's rank correlation coefficient above 0.6).
source: Moderate-to-strong positive correlations were evident for some markers, in particular IP-10 and IL-1RA, and IP-10 and VCAM-1, both with Spearman's rank correlation coefficients above 0.6 (Appendix 4—figure 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's correlation analysis, shown in Appendix 4—figure 2.

claim: In the single models, higher levels of each biomarker on illness days 1, 2, or 3 increased the risk of developing severe/moderate dengue, with the exception of ferritin in adults.
source: In the single models, higher levels of each biomarker on illness days 1, 2, or 3 increased the risk of developing S/MD, with the exception of ferritin in adults where there was a downward trend at higher values (Figure 3, Table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's single model analysis, shown in Figure 3 and Table 2.

claim: Associations between SDC-1 and the severe/moderate dengue endpoint were stronger in adults than children.
source: We observed differences between children and adults for several biomarkers, the most pronounced being SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, and IL-1RA. Associations between SDC-1 and IL-8 and the S/MD endpoint were stronger in adults than children
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis comparing children and adults.

claim: Associations between IL-8 and the severe/moderate dengue endpoint were stronger in adults than children.
source: We observed differences between children and adults for several biomarkers, the most pronounced being SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, and IL-1RA. Associations between SDC-1 and IL-8 and the S/MD endpoint were stronger in adults than children
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis comparing children and adults.

claim: The effects of IL-1RA were stronger in children than adults.
source: while the effects of IL-1RA and ferritin were stronger in children than adults.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis comparing children and adults.

claim: The effects of ferritin were stronger in children than adults.
source: while the effects of IL-1RA and ferritin were stronger in children than adults.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's analysis comparing children and adults.

claim: In the global model, SDC-1 and IL-1RA were the most stable relative to the single models for both children and adults.
source: The biomarkers SDC-1 and IL-1RA were the most stable relative to the single models for both children and adults.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's global model analysis.

claim: For IP-10 the trend of the association with severe/moderate dengue changed from positive to negative in both children and adults in the global model.
source: However, for IP-10 the trend of the association with S/MD changed from positive to negative in both children and adults.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's global model analysis.

claim: In children, VCAM-1 changed the trend from positive to weakly negative in the global model.
source: In children, VCAM-1 changed the trend from positive to weakly negative and IL-8 changed the trend from weakly positive to negative.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's global model analysis.

claim: In children, IL-8 changed the trend from weakly positive to negative in the global model.
source: In children, VCAM-1 changed the trend from positive to weakly negative and IL-8 changed the trend from weakly positive to negative.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's global model analysis.

claim: The sensitivity analysis showed that the association between the biomarkers and severe/moderate dengue did not differ between DENV-1 and other serotypes.
source: The sensitivity analysis showed that the association between the biomarkers and S/MD did not differ between DENV-1 and other serotypes (Appendix 5—figure 1; Appendix 5—figure 2; Appendix 5—table 1; Appendix 5—table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's sensitivity analysis.

claim: For children, the best subset that showed the clearest association with severe/moderate dengue was the combination of IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, ferritin, IP-10, and SDC-1 with an AIC of 465.9.
source: For children, the best subset that showed the clearest association with S/MD was the combination of the six markers IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, ferritin, IP-10, and SDC-1 with an AIC of 465.9.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: The best combination model for children was selected in 134 of the 1000 bootstrap samples.
source: This model was selected most often in the bootstrap procedure, but was not highly robust (it was selected in 134 of the 1000 samples) (Table 3, Appendix 7—table 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's bootstrap validation analysis.

claim: For children, the six variables had an inclusion frequency ranging from 73.5% for SDC-1 to 100% for IL-1RA over 1000 bootstrap samples.
source: Over the 1000 samples, the six variables had an inclusion frequency ranging from 73.5% for SDC-1 to 100% for IL-1RA.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's bootstrap validation analysis.

claim: For children, the most important biomarkers in order were IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, and ferritin.
source: The most important biomarkers in order were IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, and ferritin (Appendix 7—table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: For children, the best combination of two biomarkers was IL-1RA and ferritin.
source: The best combination of two biomarkers was IL-1RA and ferritin
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: For children, the best combinations of two and five variables were most robust with a selection percentage of 43.7% and 44%.
source: The best combinations of two and five variables were most robust with a selection percentage of 43.7% and 44%.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's bootstrap validation analysis.

claim: For adults, the best subset included SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, sTREM-1, IL-1RA, IP-10, and sCD163.
source: For adults, the best subset included the seven markers SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, sTREM-1, IL-1RA, IP-10, and sCD163.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: For adults, the best subset model was selected 79 times among 1000 bootstrap samples.
source: This model was selected 79 times among 1000 bootstrap samples, but still was selected more often than the other models (Table 4, Appendix 7—table 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's bootstrap validation analysis.

claim: For adults, the seven variables had a bootstrap inclusion frequency ranging from 59.1% for sCD163 to 99.2% for SDC-1 over 1000 samples.
source: Over the 1000 samples, the seven variables had a bootstrap inclusion frequency ranging from 59.1% for sCD163 to 99.2% for SDC-1.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's bootstrap validation analysis.

claim: For adults, the three most important biomarkers in order were SDC-1, IL-8, and ferritin.
source: The three most important biomarkers in order were SDC-1, IL-8, and ferritin (Appendix 7—table 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: For adults, the best combination of two biomarkers included SDC-1 and IL-8.
source: The best combination of two biomarkers included SDC-1 and IL-8
evidence: This is a finding from the study's variable selection analysis.

claim: For adults, the best combination of two was the most robust with a selection percentage of 56.7%.
source: The best combination of two was the most robust with a selection percentage of 56.7%, followed by the best of three variables (43.2%) (Table 4).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's bootstrap validation analysis.

claim: Clinical phenotypes of dengue in children and adults differ, with children experiencing more shock and adults more organ impairment and bleeding.
source: Clinical phenotypes of dengue in children and adults differ, with children experiencing more shock and adults more organ impairment and bleeding, with distinct clinical management guidelines published by the WHO.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about dengue, with reference to WHO guidelines.

claim: Dengue pathogenesis may differ by age.
source: Our results imply dengue pathogenesis may differ by age, with distinct combinations of immune-activation and vascular markers demonstrated between children and adults.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the study's findings about age-related differences in biomarker associations.

claim: Uncomplicated dengue in adults have higher ferritin levels compared to in children.
source: In addition, uncomplicated dengue in adults have higher ferritin levels compared to in children, with increasing age and chronic conditions in adults likely contributing to this observation.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's data analysis with inference about contributing factors.

claim: Increasing age and chronic conditions in adults likely contribute to higher ferritin levels.
source: In addition, uncomplicated dengue in adults have higher ferritin levels compared to in children, with increasing age and chronic conditions in adults likely contributing to this observation.
evidence: This is an inference about factors contributing to observed ferritin differences.

claim: Patients' age should be considered when developing biomarker panels for dengue risk prediction.
source: Hence patients' age should be considered when developing biomarker panels for dengue risk prediction.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study's findings about age-related differences.

claim: Dengue cases are forecasted to increase over the next few decades.
source: Dengue cases are forecasted to increase over the next few decades
evidence: This is a statement based on epidemiological projections, previously cited in the introduction.

claim: There is an urgent need to develop innovative methods to rapidly identify dengue patients likely to develop complications and require hospital care.
source: given the limited healthcare resources available in many endemic settings, particularly during epidemics, there is an urgent need to develop innovative methods to rapidly identify patients likely to develop complications and require hospital care (Rodriguez-Manzano et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement about clinical need, supported by a citation to Rodriguez-Manzano et al., 2018.

claim: CRP as a single biomarker was useful for early dengue diagnosis and risk identification.
source: Previously, we showed that CRP as a single biomarker was useful for early dengue diagnosis and risk identification, which is currently easy to use in all settings (Vuong et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vuong et al., 2020.

claim: Higher plasma viremia was associated with increased dengue severity regardless of age, serotype and immune status of patients.
source: Recently, we also showed that higher plasma viremia was associated with increased dengue severity regardless of age, serotype and immune status of patients (Vuong et al., 2021a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vuong et al., 2021a.

claim: The study suggests the combination of five biomarkers IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, ferritin, and IP-10 for children to be used in practice.
source: To be more applicable by balancing model fit, robustness, and parsimony, we suggest the combination of five biomarkers IL-1RA, Ang-2, IL-8, ferritin, and IP-10 for children
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study's findings, balancing statistical considerations.

claim: The study suggests the combination of three biomarkers SDC-1, IL-8, and ferritin for adults to be used in practice.
source: and the combination of three biomarkers SDC-1, IL-8, and ferritin for adults to be used in practice.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study's findings, balancing statistical considerations.

claim: The suggested combinations had a similar AIC with the best combinations (the difference of AIC was less than 5).
source: These combinations had a similar AIC with the best combinations (the difference of AIC was less than 5), but they required fewer number of biomarkers in a test panel.
evidence: This is a finding from the study's statistical analysis comparing model performance.

claim: With the advent of novel technologies including microarray platforms and multiplex lateral flow assays, the cost is likely to come down in the future.
source: With the advent of novel technologies including microarray platforms and multiplex lateral flow assays, the cost is likely to come down in the future, allowing for wide-spread use in low-to-middle-income countries.
evidence: This is a speculation about future technological developments and their impact on cost.

claim: The study adopted a data-driven 'best subset' approach for variable selection.
source: We adopted a data-driven 'best subset' approach which we think offers advantages over other methods, given the complexity of the biomarkers involved and their interactions.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology used.

claim: Other approaches for variable selection yielded results very similar to the best subset procedure.
source: We also explored other approaches for variable selection (Heinze et al., 2018; Piironen and Vehtari, 2017; Sauerbrei et al., 2020) and the results were very similar to the best subset procedure (Appendix 9—table 1; Appendix 9—table 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the study's sensitivity analysis comparing different statistical methods.

claim: The study used a nested case-control dataset from a prospective multi-country cohort study with consistent data collection and standardized outcome definitions and laboratory methodologies.
source: Strengths of our study include the large sample size and use of a nested case-control dataset from a prospective multi-country cohort study with consistent data collection and standardized outcome definitions and laboratory methodologies.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study design and methodology.

claim: The biomarker panel was selected based on pathogenesis studies, focusing on pathways activated early in the disease course.
source: The biomarker panel we selected was guided by pathogenesis studies, focusing on pathways activated early in the disease course, thus ensuring clinical relevance.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the rationale for biomarker selection.

claim: The study analysed the biomarkers at only one time-point in the early phase.
source: One being we analysed the biomarkers at only one time-point in the early phase; limited financial resources did not allow us to evaluate the full range of biomarkers across the whole IDAMS population and at more time-points.
evidence: This is a direct statement about a study limitation.

claim: The study was not designed to build prediction models.
source: Secondly, this study was not designed to build prediction models so we did not use a measure of predictive value as a criterion, which was motivated by the nested case-control design.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study design and its limitations.

claim: The findings need to be validated in new studies.
source: Our findings need to be validated in new studies.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the need for external validation.

claim: Higher levels of the ten biomarkers (VCAM-1, SDC-1, Ang-2, IL-8, IP-10, IL-1RA, sCD163, sTREM-1, ferritin, and CRP), when considered individually, are associated with increased risk of adverse clinical outcomes in both children and adults with dengue.
source: In conclusion, higher levels of the ten biomarkers (VCAM-1, SDC-1, Ang-2, IL-8, IP-10, IL-1RA, sCD163, sTREM-1, ferritin, and CRP), when considered individually, are associated with increased risk of adverse clinical outcomes in both children and adults with dengue.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: These findings serve to assist the development of biomarker panels to improve future triage and early assessment of dengue patients.
source: These findings serve to assist the development of biomarker panels to improve future triage and early assessment of dengue patients.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential application of the study's findings.

claim: The findings could aid individual patient management and facilitate healthcare allocation which would be of major public health benefit especially in outbreak settings.
source: This would aid not only individual patient management and facilitate healthcare allocation which would be of major public health benefit especially in outbreak settings, but could also serve as potential biological endpoints for dengue clinical trials.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential public health impact of the study's findings.

claim: The findings could serve as potential biological endpoints for dengue clinical trials.
source: This would aid not only individual patient management and facilitate healthcare allocation which would be of major public health benefit especially in outbreak settings, but could also serve as potential biological endpoints for dengue clinical trials.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential application of the study's findings in clinical research.

claim: The IDAMS study was performed in eight countries across Asia and Latin America.
source: The IDAMS study was performed in eight countries across Asia and Latin America.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's geographic scope, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: For this study, cases were selected in four countries (Vietnam, Cambodia, Malaysia, and El Salvador) as the blood samples were stored at the laboratory of the Oxford University Clinical Research Unit in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
source: For this study, we selected cases in four countries (Vietnam, Cambodia, Malaysia, and El Salvador) as the blood samples were stored at the laboratory of the Oxford University Clinical Research Unit in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the sample selection rationale, also shown in Figure 1.

claim: Of the 2694 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases in the IDAMS study, 38 and 266 cases were classified as severe and moderate dengue respectively.
source: Of the 2694 laboratory-confirmed dengue cases in the IDAMS study, 38 and 266 cases were classified as severe and moderate dengue respectively.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the case distribution in the parent study.

claim: The biomarkers were measured at two time points: at enrollment (illness day 1–3) and after recovery (day 10–31 post-symptom onset).
source: The biomarkers were measured at two time points: at enrollment (illness day 1–3) and after recovery (day 10–31 post-symptom onset), if available.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the timing of biomarker measurements.

claim: Eight biomarkers (CRP and ferritin excepted) were combined in a premixed magnetic bead panel.
source: Eight biomarkers (CRP and ferritin excepted) were combined in a premixed magnetic bead panel (Cat No. LXSAHM; R and D).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the laboratory methodology.

claim: CRP was measured using a separate commercial magnetic bead panel.
source: CRP was measured using a separate commercial magnetic bead panel (Cat. No. HCVD3MAG-67K; EMD Millipore Corporation).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the laboratory methodology.

claim: Ferritin was measured using the Human Ferritin ELISA kit.
source: Ferritin was measured using the Human Ferritin ELISA kit (Cat. No. ARG80501, Arigo).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the laboratory methodology.

claim: The primary endpoint was combined severe and moderate dengue (S/MD).
source: The primary endpoint was combined severe and moderate dengue (S/MD), defined by the development of severe or moderate grades of any of the following – plasma leakage, haemorrhage, or organ impairment (including neurologic, hepatic, or cardiac involvement) (Appendix 2—table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's primary endpoint definition.

claim: Severe and moderate dengue were combined to form the primary endpoint because severe dengue events were rare.
source: We combined severe and moderate dengue to form the primary endpoint (S/MD) as severe dengue events were rare; this combined endpoint is relevant to clinical practice since the moderate group is likely to develop complications and therefore may also require medical intervention and hospitalization.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the rationale for the endpoint definition.

claim: The moderate dengue group is likely to develop complications and may require medical intervention and hospitalization.
source: this combined endpoint is relevant to clinical practice since the moderate group is likely to develop complications and therefore may also require medical intervention and hospitalization.
evidence: This is a statement about clinical characteristics of moderate dengue, based on clinical knowledge.

claim: Three secondary endpoints were studied: severe dengue alone, severe dengue or dengue with warning signs according to the 2009 WHO classification, and hospitalization.
source: We studied three secondary endpoints: severe dengue alone, severe dengue or dengue with warning signs according to the 2009 WHO classification, and hospitalization.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the study's secondary endpoints.

claim: The decision to hospitalize was based only on clinical judgement and local guidelines particular to each study site, without use of any biomarker information.
source: The decision to hospitalize was based only on clinical judgement and local guidelines particular to each study site, without use of any biomarker information.
evidence: This is a direct statement about how hospitalization decisions were made in the study.

claim: Plasma levels of all biomarkers were transformed to the base-2 logarithm (log-2) before analysis.
source: Plasma levels of all biomarkers were transformed to the base-2 logarithm (log-2) before analysis as a right skewed distribution was apparent.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: A logistic regression model was used for all endpoints.
source: We used a logistic regression model for all endpoints.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: The study investigated the non-linear effects of all biomarkers and age on the endpoints, using restricted cubic splines with three knots.
source: We investigated the non-linear effects of all biomarkers and age on the endpoints, using restricted cubic splines with three knots at the 10th, 50th, and 90th percentiles.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: Variable selection was based on the 'best subset' approach.
source: We used variable selection based on the 'best subset' approach (Hastie et al., 2017; Hocking and Leslie, 1967).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology, supported by citations.

claim: The best subset approach screened all possible combinations of biomarkers and selected the best based on the Akaike information criterion (AIC).
source: Briefly, this approach screened all possible combinations of biomarkers and selected the best based on the Akaike information criterion (AIC).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the statistical methodology.

claim: AIC was chosen as a ranking measurement because it quantifies goodness of fit, while guarding against over-fitting.
source: We chose AIC as a ranking measurement because it quantifies goodness of fit, while guarding against over-fitting.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the rationale for the statistical approach.

claim: A bootstrap procedure was performed to check the robustness (stability) of the selected models.
source: We then performed a bootstrap procedure to check the robustness (stability) of the selected models.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the validation methodology.

claim: The bootstrap procedure resampled 1000 times with replacement from the original dataset.
source: For this we resampled 1000 times with replacement from the original dataset.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the validation methodology.

claim: The association of IP-10 with severe/moderate dengue may have changed because another biomarker in the model is a mediator or confounder of IP-10 in the pathway to the outcome.
source: Particularly, the association of IP-10 with S/MD changed significantly from the single to global model, which may be because another biomarker in our model is a mediator or confounder of IP-10 in the pathway to the outcome.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism underlying the observed change in association.

claim: IL-1RA could be a mediator or confounder of IP-10 because its association with severe/moderate dengue was similar between the single and global model, and the correlation between IP-10 and IL-1RA was strong (Spearman's rank correlation coefficient was 0.75).
source: This could be IL-1RA as its association with S/MD was similar between the single and global model, and the correlation between IP-10 and IL-1RA was strong (Spearman's rank correlation coefficient was 0.75).
evidence: This is an inference about the relationship between biomarkers, based on data analysis.

claim: Changing the direction of the association from the single to global model does not diminish the possibility of that biomarker being selected in the best combinations.
source: Nonetheless, changing the direction of the association from the single to global model does not diminish the possibility of that biomarker being selected in the best combinations.
evidence: This is an inference about the interpretation of the statistical findings.

claim: The difference in IL-8 and ferritin associations between children and adults is likely due to the composite endpoint of severe and moderate dengue.
source: Specifically, the association of IL-8 and ferritin differed between children and adults, which is likely to be due to the composite endpoint of severe and moderate dengue.
evidence: This is an inference about the reason for observed differences, based on further analysis.

claim: The effects of IL-8 and ferritin were similar in children and adults for severe dengue alone.
source: As shown in the analysis of severe dengue alone (Appendix 4—figure 1, Appendix 4—table 1), the effects of IL-8 and ferritin were similar in children and adults
evidence: This is a finding from a secondary analysis.

claim: IL-8 and ferritin are still associated with severe disease in all age groups.
source: which suggests these biomarkers are still associated with severe disease in all age groups and that the difference is driven by the moderate dengue group.
evidence: This is an inference based on the secondary analysis findings.

claim: The difference in IL-8 and ferritin associations is driven by the moderate dengue group.
source: which suggests these biomarkers are still associated with severe disease in all age groups and that the difference is driven by the moderate dengue group.
evidence: This is an inference based on the secondary analysis findings.

claim: In the sensitivity analysis, viremia was not selected in any of the best combinations for children.
source: In the sensitivity analysis, viremia was not selected in any of the best combinations for children, and the marker combinations remained the same as the main analysis.
evidence: This is a finding from the sensitivity analysis.

claim: For adults in the sensitivity analysis, the best subset included five markers SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, viremia and sCD163.
source: For adults, the best subset included five markers SDC-1, IL-8, ferritin, viremia and sCD163.
evidence: This is a finding from the sensitivity analysis.

claim: In some of the cases the biomarkers did not return to normal at convalescence.
source: In some of the cases the biomarkers did not return to normal at convalescence.
evidence: This is an observation from the study's data analysis.

claim: Male gender was predominant (60% and 54% in the case and control groups respectively).
source: Male gender was predominant (60% and 54% in the case and control groups respectively).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the demographic characteristics of the study population.

claim: The severe/moderate dengue group had a slightly lower percentage of obese patients than the control group (10% versus 14%).
source: The S/MD had a slightly lower percentage of obese patients than the control group (10% versus 14%).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the clinical characteristics of the study groups.

claim: Most of the moderate dengue cases were plasma leakage and/or hepatic involvement.
source: Most of the moderate dengue cases were plasma leakage and/or hepatic involvement (Appendix 4—table 1).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the clinical manifestations, with reference to a table.
